newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan sacks second provincial government.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sacks second provincial government.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari sacked a second provincial government on Friday to clear the decks for fresh elections he has promised in February after dismissing prime minister Benazir Bhutto.
The governor of the southwestern province of Baluchistan dissolved the local parliament on presidential orders.
The move came as Bhutto prepared to launch a two-pronged campaign to recapture power, fighting her Tuesday dismissal in court and taking her cause to the streets.

The Baluchistan government of Chief Minister Zulfikar Ali Magsi ceased to exist after the dissolution of the 43-member provincial assembly by provincial governor Imranullah Khan, state radio quoted a government notification issued in the provincial capital Quetta as saying.
The move in Pakistan's largest but least populated province, which borders Iran and Afghanistan, came a day after similar action in the country's most industrialised province of Sindh.

There was no immediate announcement of a new caretaker chief minister to replace Magsi, a tribal chief and member of the anti-Bhutto Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party, who headed a 31-member coalition government of various parties.
On Tuesday Leghari dissolved the lower house of Pakistan's parliament. He sacked Bhutto on disputed charges of corruption and misrule and ordered fresh elections for February 3.
Political sources said the dissolution of assemblies in Pakistan's two other provinces -- Punjab and North West Frontier -- would be ordered any time.

The grounds cited for the action in Baluchistan were similar to those given for sacking Bhutto and the Sindh government of her Pakistan People's Party (PPP). They included alleged corruption, misrule and violation of laws.
Most members of the Baluchistan cabinet had earlier spoken against a dissolution of the assembly and some said they would go to court if it were carried out.
Bhutto said on Thursday night she expected to file a legal challenge next week to Leghari's order toppling her government.
She promised to tour the country to whip up support for the PPP, now that the four-day-old caretaker government had lifted curbs on her movements.
"I am going to fight back," Bhutto told Reuters Television in an interview.
She was expected to meet advisers on Friday to discuss the court challenge to Leghari's order, which she called illegal and unconstitutional.
